layers.note: A leading herb of subalpine meadows, forming broad patches.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −12 to 8 °C; gone below −18 °C and above 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −32 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −40 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 22 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 5,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 3,500 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.4, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.65.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Broadleaf lupine grows from British Columbia to California, lowlands to subalpine meadows (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
